resources.string: Keyboard X Privacy Policy
Last updated: October 14, 2026 | Version 1.0

This Privacy Policy explains how Keyboard X handles information when you install, configure, and use the application and its Android keyboard service. It is intended to describe the current product responsibly and must be reviewed whenever the application's code, permissions, integrations, or data practices change. Please read this policy before enabling Keyboard X as an input method.
1. Scope of This Policy

This policy applies to the Keyboard X Android application, its settings screens, and its keyboard input method service distributed as part of the same product. It covers information that may be processed while the application runs, while the keyboard is enabled, and when you contact support. It does not automatically apply to third-party applications, websites, operating-system services, or email providers that you choose to use. Those services operate under their own privacy terms and policies.
2. Our Privacy Principles

Keyboard X is designed to provide an on-device typing interface and configuration experience. Privacy explanations must remain consistent with the actual software shipped to users. We do not treat a feature as private merely because it is intended to be private, and we do not claim that information is never collected, transmitted, or stored unless the released implementation has been examined and supports that statement. If a future version introduces analytics, diagnostics, online services, advertising, cloud processing, or account features, this policy must be updated before those changes are released.
3. Information You Type

An input method processes key input and text-editing events so that Android applications can receive the characters you enter. Depending on the field and the behavior of the receiving application, this can involve ordinary text, names, messages, search terms, or other content. Text entered through a keyboard can be highly personal. The precise information processed depends on the active keyboard implementation, the text field, Android behavior, and the application in which you type. You should never assume that all text fields are risk-free.
4. Passwords and Sensitive Information

Passwords, payment details, authentication codes, private messages, health information, financial information, and other sensitive content deserve particular care. Follow Android and the receiving application's indications about secure fields. Do not enter sensitive information into an unfamiliar keyboard or on a device you do not trust. A keyboard may be able to process text input as part of its core function, but that fact alone does not establish whether a particular version stores, transmits, or retains that text. Those questions must be answered from the actual implementation and any applicable system behavior.
5. Keyboard Input and Data Transmission

The keyboard's input-processing behavior must be evaluated from the released source code, Android permissions, dependencies, and runtime behavior. This policy does not make an unsupported guarantee that typed content can never leave the device. Before public release, the project owner should verify whether the keyboard service or any included library performs network requests, uploads diagnostic information, sends usage events, or transfers typed content. Any such behavior must be disclosed accurately, including its purpose, legal basis where applicable, recipients, retention period, and available user choices.
6. App Settings and Preferences

The application may use Android storage mechanisms to retain settings needed for its features, where those settings are implemented. Examples may include an application appearance choice, language preference, keyboard theme, or sound preference. The exact settings retained by a particular release depend on the code in that release. Local storage on your device is different from a remote server, but local storage can still be accessible through certain device-management, backup, debugging, or compromised-device scenarios. Use your device's security controls and keep Android updated.
7. Information You Provide to Support

If you choose to report a problem through the in-app report form, the form can prepare an email addressed to dmolgax@gmail.com. The current report form asks for a contact email address, a problem category, and a description; a name is optional. The form validates the required fields before preparing the email. The email application is opened so that you can review, edit, and send the message yourself. Opening the email composer does not itself mean that a report has been sent or received.
8. Email Providers and Support Messages

When you send a support email, your chosen email provider and the recipient's email provider process the message under their own policies and technical systems. The message may contain the contact information and problem description you choose to provide. Email may be retained in sent folders, inboxes, backups, spam filters, or provider systems. Do not include passwords, verification codes, payment card numbers, or other unnecessary sensitive information in a support request. We cannot control the privacy practices or security of a third-party email service that you select.
9. Information We Ask You Not to Send

Please do not include account passwords, one-time authentication codes, full payment card details, government identity numbers, private encryption keys, or confidential information belonging to another person in a support report. If a technical issue requires an example, provide a minimal example with real names, addresses, account details, and private message content removed. Only share information that is necessary to explain the issue and that you are comfortable sending by email.
10. Permissions and Android System Access

Android input methods require users to enable the keyboard through system settings before it can be used as an input method. Android may display system warnings explaining the capabilities of an enabled keyboard. Review those warnings carefully and only enable a keyboard you trust. The application must request only permissions needed for its implemented features. The permissions declared in the released AndroidManifest.xml, including any permissions added by dependencies, should be reviewed before publication. This policy does not substitute for the operating system's permission screens or security notices.
11. Third-Party Applications

Keyboard X is used in combination with other applications, websites, and Android system components. The receiving application determines how it handles text after Android delivers input to it. For example, a messaging application may transmit a message when you choose to send it, and a browser may send search terms when you submit a search. Those actions are controlled by the receiving application and your choices, not by this policy. Review the privacy terms of applications and services in which you type.
12. Analytics, Advertising, and Tracking

This policy must disclose any analytics, advertising, attribution, tracking, crash-reporting, or measurement technology actually included in the released product. No such feature should be assumed to exist or to be absent without reviewing the build configuration, source code, dependencies, and runtime behavior. If one is added in a future release, this section must identify the relevant data categories, purposes, providers, retention practices, and choices available to users before the feature is distributed.
13. Network Services and Cloud Processing

Any future network-connected feature must be assessed separately before release. If a version sends information to a remote service, the policy must explain what is sent, why it is needed, when the transfer occurs, who operates the service, how long the information is kept, and whether it is shared with additional recipients. If typed text is ever processed remotely, that fact must be clearly disclosed and the product must provide any consent or controls required by applicable law. A feature must not be described as on-device-only if it depends on remote processing.
14. Data Sharing and Recipients

Any disclosure about sharing must reflect actual product behavior and actual service providers. Information may be handled by a recipient when you deliberately send it, such as when you submit a support email. Other disclosures, if introduced, must be described with their purposes and legal requirements. This policy does not authorize unrelated use of your information. Before adding third-party SDKs, advertising partners, crash services, cloud systems, or analytics providers, the project owner should assess their access to data and update the policy accordingly.
15. Data Retention

Information stored locally may remain on your device until you change a setting, clear the application's data, uninstall the application, or Android removes it under its own storage rules. Exact retention behavior depends on the type of data and the implementation. Support emails may remain in your email account and the recipient's account according to the providers' retention practices. If remote storage is introduced in a future version, the policy must state the relevant retention periods or criteria and explain how deletion requests are handled.
16. Deletion and User Controls

You can disable Keyboard X through Android's keyboard-management settings. Android's application settings may also provide options to clear locally stored application data or uninstall the app. These actions do not necessarily delete emails already sent, information retained by an email provider, backups, or records controlled by another service. Where a future version stores personal information remotely, appropriate deletion and access procedures should be documented and implemented in accordance with applicable law.
17. Children's Privacy

Keyboard X is not intended to encourage children to disclose personal information. Parents and guardians should supervise device setup and keyboard selection when appropriate. If the product is distributed to children or is directed to a child audience in a particular jurisdiction, additional legal obligations may apply. The product owner must evaluate applicable age-related requirements before distribution and must not rely on this general statement as a substitute for those requirements.
18. Security

Reasonable security practices should be used to protect the application code, release process, support mailbox, and any information handled by the product. No application, device, email system, or transmission method can be guaranteed completely secure. Users should keep their devices updated, use screen locks and other appropriate protections, install software from trusted sources, and review Android's keyboard warnings. If a security incident affects personal information, the response and any required notices must follow applicable law.
19. International Processing

If support messages or future service data are processed by providers operating in different countries, the information may be handled in jurisdictions with different privacy laws. Any cross-border processing introduced by the product must be assessed and disclosed where required. The current email workflow depends in part on the email service selected by the user, and that provider's terms govern its handling of the message.
20. Changes to This Policy

This policy may need to change when the application adds or removes features, changes its permissions, integrates new libraries, introduces network functionality, or becomes subject to new legal requirements. A revised policy should identify its effective date and explain material changes in understandable language. Where applicable law requires notice or consent for a change, the product owner must provide it. Continuing to display an outdated policy after a material change can mislead users and should be avoided.
21. Legal Rights and Applicable Law

Your privacy rights depend on your location and the laws that apply to the product and its operator. Depending on those laws and the circumstances, rights may include requesting access to personal information, correcting it, requesting deletion, objecting to certain processing, or submitting a complaint to a competent authority. These rights may be subject to exceptions and verification requirements. The product owner should obtain appropriate legal advice before making jurisdiction-specific promises in this policy.
22. Contact About Privacy

For questions or concerns about this policy or the handling of information by Keyboard X, contact the support address at dmolgax@gmail.com. Describe your concern clearly and avoid including passwords, authentication codes, or other unnecessary sensitive information. Sending an email is a voluntary action, and the email provider you use will process that message under its own policies.
23. Product Accuracy and Release Review

This policy is a product document and must be maintained alongside the software. Before publication, the release owner should inspect the input method service, all activities, manifest permissions, storage code, network libraries, build dependencies, and any automated collection or reporting functionality. The owner should also test the final release rather than relying only on source-level assumptions. If the implementation differs from the statements in this policy, the code or the policy must be corrected before release.
24. Your Informed Choice

Installing the application does not remove your responsibility to make informed choices about the keyboard you enable. Read the system's warnings, review the features available in your version, and decide whether the keyboard meets your privacy needs. You may choose not to enable it or may disable it later through Android settings. If you are unsure how a particular release handles a category of information, seek clarification before entering sensitive content.

This policy should be read together with the Keyboard X Terms of Use and the information displayed by Android. It is not a guarantee that every device, third-party application, or email provider behaves identically. The final public policy must be checked against the exact version distributed to users and the legal requirements applicable to its release.
